description_full: Adyen N.V. operates a payments platform in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North America, the Asia Pacific, and Latin America. Its platform integrates payments stack, including gateway, risk management, processing, acquiring, and settlement services. The company offers a back-end infrastructure for authorizing. It accepts payment through online, in-person payments, cross channel, and Adyen for Platforms. The company also provides optimization services, including Adyen Uplift, protect, authenticate and tokenize. In addition, it offers financial products, such as accounts, capital, issuing, and payouts. It serves digital, mobility, SaaS platforms, retail, food and beverages, subscription, and travel and hospitality businesses. The company was incorporated in 2006 and is based in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.
ceo_bio: Mr. Pieter Willem van der Does | Co-Founder, Co- CEO & Member of Management Board | Age 56 | Compensation: $976,935 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 5K people. Revenue per employee of $581K ranks in the above the sector median among Technology peers. Each employee generates $199K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $9K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Adyen N.V. is a large-cap technology business with a $29.4B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -32% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +11.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Gross margins of 88% are the starting point for assessing pricing power.

The business throws off $998M in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.97× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 56× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 0.1% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

news_headlines.title: Adyen (OTCMKTS:ADYYF) Stock Falls 0.9% – Time to Sell?

sect: Its 41% operating margin runs 35pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.77x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 36% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 46% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 70% and a beta of 1.37, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.04 vs 5y 1.68), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $112K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 28% in the 2020 crash and 55% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $828 (margin of safety -12%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 33%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $733 to $965 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: EV/EBITDA 13.5 vs 17.1 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 6.3% annual cash-flow growth, 3pp more than the model expects.
prof: It runs a 88% gross margin and converts 34% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 20% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.3x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 17% last year, worth watching.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $11.3B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.8, in the safe zone).
The Beneish M-score (-1.88) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -31.8% over 3 years.
own: Insiders own 13.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 78%.
people: With about 5,020 employees, each generates about $581K of revenue, 1.6x the Technology median.
That works out to $199K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $977K (2x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
